A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LARM/Minecraft research, despite substantial methodological revision. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable. V1's appendices A–J were inspected and matched against retained or relocated material in v2, which has no appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original LARM task-success rates, inference timings, augmentation ablations, qualitative experiments and an appendix training-data-volume study.

after.justification: V2 reports original MineDojo and Mineflayer evaluations, reward-design and backbone ablations, and model question-answer examples, particularly in Tables 1–4 and Section 5.

M1.justification: V1 trains a LLaVA-based 7B skill predictor using Wiki pretraining and the annotated ARTNS dataset with three augmentations. V2 replaces this training approach with online PPO and an LLM referee supplying four-category auxiliary rewards. Its TinyLLaVA-3.1B architecture introduces an input skill token and separate action and critic heads. These change the architecture, objectives and learning procedure.

E1.justification: V1's manually collected 2,589-example ARTNS training corpus is replaced by online exploration, while the 34G Wiki source remains. V2 evaluates LARM using both MineDojo's RL-based skills and Mineflayer's API-based skills; v1's LARM uses the API skill library even when compared with MineDojo baselines. The village, Nether and cooperative-combat scenarios already occur in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Most main comparators remain. Table 1 adds RL-GPT, while Table 2 removes ReAct and Reflexion but retains AutoGPT, Voyager and STEVE. V1's matched LLaVA inference-time comparison also disappears, and the supplementary LLM question-answer comparison changes model membership.

E3.justification: V2 establishes separate evaluation protocols: MineDojo uses RL-based skills and initial tools, while Mineflayer uses API skills and empty inventories. The principal backbone changes from 7B to 3.1B, with an additional 0.5B ablation. Reported latency uses RTX4090 rather than RTX3090 hardware, and v1's controlled 100-case, equal-size model timing experiment is no longer presented.

E4.justification: V1's augmentation ablations, appendix data-volume study and multi-view qualitative analyses are removed. V2 adds reward-source, two-versus-four-category feedback and backbone-size ablations. Wiki pretraining is examined through task-success rates and a new question-answer example rather than the earlier convergence plot and horse-combat example. V1's appendix case studies are retained in v2 Section 5.4 and Figure 3, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly increases LARM's Mineflayer evaluation from three to thirty trials to reduce randomness; baseline results remain based on three trials. Shared ordinary tasks in Table 1 already used thirty trials in v1. Neither version supplies confidence intervals, significance tests or independent training-seed variability.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces v1's near-universal 1.00 LARM success rates with results including 0.93 for sticks and 0.27 for iron swords under the revised MineDojo setup. Table 2 changes diamond and enchanted achievement results from 3/3 and 2/3 to 28/30 and 16/30. New reward/backbone results replace earlier ablations. Reported latency changes from 0.85 seconds to 0.58 seconds with different model and hardware settings; these are not controlled cross-version performance changes.

T1.justification: V2 adds an MDP formulation, actor–critic objectives, generalized advantage estimation and a mathematical argument for vanishing long-horizon feedback in Sections 3–4 and Equations 1–6. It also defines ordered referee rewards. V1 contains no corresponding RL formalization or reward-vanishment derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from ARTNS data organization, collection and augmentation to referee RL and learning through online interaction without human supervision. V2 adds claims of mathematically identifying feedback vanishment and pioneering online RL optimization of an LLM-style embodied policy. The enchanted-equipment achievement remains, while the prominent 6.8× speedup claim is replaced by lightweight-model and real-time-inference claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains performance chiefly through referee feedback, distinguishing correct actions from successful outcomes, and attributes longer-task failures to vanishing feedback. This replaces v1's emphasis on augmentation-based scheduling and multi-view recipe selection. V2 also omits v1's explicit limitation that LARM was tested in Minecraft without real-world deployment.

D1.justification: V1 provides image and embedding dimensions, learning rates, batch size, training epochs, Wiki preprocessing, input examples and skill code. Much of this documentation disappears, including details of the retained Wiki pretraining stage. V2 adds RL pseudocode, referee input descriptions and approximately 42 hours of exploration on one RTX4090, but leaves numerical auxiliary rewards and the exact referee prompt unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 introduces a substantial RL-with-LLMs discussion, positioning referee judgments against skill scheduling and reward-code generation. New references include PPO, RL-GPT, Text2Reward and TinyLLaVA. Much of v1's general embodied-benchmark and robotics discussion is removed, and novelty is repositioned around online RL rather than chiefly action-output ambiguity and training-data organization.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments and conclusion are extensively rewritten around reinforcement learning. V1's separate Algorithm and Data and Training sections become Preliminary and Method sections. The contents page and dedicated appendices disappear, with selected baseline descriptions and case studies integrated into the main text.

P2.justification: V2 changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, redraws the overview and architecture figures around RL, and adds an algorithm block. Most data, augmentation, multi-view and pretraining illustrations disappear; tables are reorganized for the revised comparisons and ablations. V1 Figure 10 is retained and relocated as v2 Figure 3.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evaluation through separate MineDojo/Mineflayer comparisons, thirty-trial Mineflayer testing and targeted reward ablations. However, it removes substantial implementation detail and leaves its new central RL procedure underspecified. The formal description also contains inconsistencies: Algorithm 1 supplies a future action to the referee where Section 4.1 specifies the next state. These gains in empirical assessment coexist with weaker reproducibility and unresolved formal clarity, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
